decisions.reason: As a classic door lever handle it is relatively easy to keep in the portfolio and supports range completeness, but its more standard character and overlap with other handle launches make it the most pruneable if early demand disappoints.

A door lever handle family fits the firm's system-breadth strategy and can serve multiple project types, so management would usually keep the option open while market acceptance across specifications becomes clearer.
A new door handle design matches the firm's design-led positioning and likely has modest continuation costs, so it would normally be retained at least another year unless feedback is clearly weak.
This design variant extends architectural choice and brand presence, and in a growing market a large German supplier would usually wait longer before abandoning such a low-cost option.

Another door lever handle family strengthens coverage across complexity and budget levels, which is central to the firm's strategy, so the firm is likely to continue observing sales before deciding on withdrawal.

The electronic access system is a flagship product directly aligned with the firm's move toward digital building organization, so real-options logic strongly favors keeping and learning from it rather than exiting early.
